reading.body:
Google operates a data center campus in Berkeley County, Moncks Corner, South Carolina, one of its original long-running US sites. The operator does not publish megawatt capacity, square footage, or building-level specifications for individual facilities on its data center location pages, so this campus's IT load is not disclosed.

Google announced a $500 million expansion specific to Moncks Corner and a combined $3.3 billion expansion across its two South Carolina campuses in September 2024. These investment figures place the site among Google's material infrastructure bets but do not specify how much of the capital goes to power and cooling versus buildings, nor do they translate to current or target megawatts. The state context shows 14 mapped data center facilities across South Carolina, of which only four operators publish power capacity, totaling 6.6 MW of disclosed IT load statewide.

Without published megawatt figures for this campus, its rank among sites that matter to AI scaling cannot be read from power consumption. The scale of Google's capital commitment and the site's tenure suggest it is a significant part of Google's fleet, but the absence of disclosed capacity means this campus cannot be placed in the state or national infrastructure hierarchy by the metric that binds AI compute to the grid.
